notes:
The ambience is re-recorded. Every track is now a two minute loop cut from the original recording at four times the detail, in stereo, instead of forty-five minutes squeezed into a thirty-second-rate encode. Night city, Cafe and Morning sea were scratchy because the top two octaves were simply gone, which is where birdsong, traffic and crockery live, and they are back. The loop is cut from the calmest stretch of each recording and the join is measured to be no quieter than anywhere else in the track, so it comes round without announcing itself. Adrift used to fade into silence exactly where it looped; it no longer does. All of this made the app about fifty megabytes smaller.

Volume is fixed in three ways. Every track is levelled to the same loudness as it is encoded, so none of them is louder than another any more. Three of them had never been levelled at all. And the slider is a loudness control now rather than a straight line, so the quiet end is usable and the top is not painful.

Morning sea is Sunset Beach, and it brings the whole look with it: the sunset, the tide and the sky, not just the colours. The Adrift track is called Deep space for the same reason. Both looks have left the themes shop, because they were in two places at once; if you had bought either, you still have it.

The skyline has depth. The towers stand at different distances now, with air between them, and the far ones sway less than the near ones instead of all drifting the same amount. First frost falls mostly as soft dots with a cut crystal here and there, rather than the other way round. The spiders' corner webs run off the top and sides of the screen instead of stopping in mid air.

Signed in, the corner shows a small profile mark rather than your name, which used to collide with the app's own name on a phone. The sign in box is a real form, so your phone and your password manager recognise it and can fill and save it. A wrong password says so in red.

Starting the app no longer flashes a white screen with somebody else's logo on it.

And on the main screen, the minutes could stop following the buttons if anything else on the page had failed to draw. They cannot any more.
